Theme

Latin word

solidus

solidus, solida, solidum

declension

solid: dense, not hollow; firm; whole, entire, not in parts

In this lexicon

  • solid

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Top. 22: pariēs vel solidus vel fornicātus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Div. 1.48: a solid gold column, against a gilded one (Lewis & Short)

  • whole

    also used · classical · Plin. NH 8.36: ut solidōs hauriant cervōs taurōsque (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 6.253: solida taurōrum vīscera (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • nam etiam maximum solida nōn recēpērunt, rūrsus ārida et corripī facilia scintillam quoque fovent ūsque in incendium

    for solid logs won’t take even a great flame, while dry stuff that catches easily nurses even a spark into a blazeSen. Ep. 18.15

    In the entry for solid

  • perque coāgula dēnsa liquor in solidum coit

    and with thick rennet the liquid sets solidPrud. Cath. 3.66–70
